title: Model landscape signal hunting and prioritization rubric
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a repeatable playbook and lightweight automation to discover, score, and prioritize emerging open-models and closed-model variants that matter for Redwood’s product roadmap and serving economics. Deliverables: scoring rubric, data ingestion pipeline (public artifacts + signals), prioritization dashboard, and handoff to roadmap owners.
background: Recent spikes in interest for quantized LoRA adapters and several new 7B and 13B open checkpoints require a consistent way to decide which models to validate for runtime compatibility, quantization profiles, and Dedicated sizing. Current research notes are ad-hoc and there is no single source of truth for candidate models or priority signals.
goals: Define scoring rubric with axes for quality, cost/latency, integration effort, adoption momentum, licensing/risk
Implement automated harvesting of public signals (GitHub stars, Hugging Face downloads, PapersWithCode citations) and internal signals (trial usage, eval delta, regression alerts)
Surface top 10 candidate models weekly in a dashboard and weekly digest to Eng/Research/PM
Produce 2 validated model onboarding pilots by the due date with clear owner and rollout plan
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented in Confluence with weighting rationale and example scores
ETL pipeline (airflow job) populates model tracker sheet with at least 6 signal types every 24h
Dashboard created in Looker showing top-N by composite score and change-over-time
Two pilot models selected and assigned to Runtime + Research with acceptance test plans
milestones: M1: Rubric draft and stakeholder review - 2026-02-28
M2: Minimal ETL + seed model list (30 models) - 2026-03-07
M3: Dashboard v0 and weekly digest - 2026-03-21
M4: Pilot validation start for first model - 2026-03-28
updates: 2026-02-23: Kickoff with Research and Runtime. Agreed on initial axes: Quality (evals), Cost (perf bench), Momentum (community signals), Integration Effort (tokenizer/architecture quirks), Legal Risk (license).
2026-03-01: Research delivered first-pass eval delta matrix for 24 open models. Noted two 13B variants with atypical state dict layouts that may need model-origin adapters.
2026-03-04: Eng spike found that one high-momentum 7B requires attention due to non-standard kv-cache layout. Marked as "potential blocker" for quick-onboard. Logged ENG-2726 as follow-up.
2026-03-08: Product review: reduced weight for GitHub stars after discussion — community signals are noisy for short-lived trends. Decided to add a persistence metric (downloads over 30d).
2026-03-10: Dashboard v0 prototype shared (link below). Requested Looker owner and read access for PM/Research/Runtime. Next: wire trial-usage signal from hosted API to tracker.
decisions: Adopt composite scoring with configurable weights; default weights: Quality 35%, Cost 25%, Momentum 20%, Integration Effort 15%, Legal Risk 5%
Source-of-truth will be a Google Sheet for now to enable rapid iteration; ETL will write there and Looker will read from the sheet via a scheduled export
Start with public signals: HF downloads, HF recent commits, GH stars, Twitter mentions (filtered), PapersWithCode links, and low-latency internal trial usage. Add more later.
Do not automatically deprecate models based only on a single signal dip; require 2-3 signal confirmations before marking as dropped
tradeoffs: Automation vs. accuracy: Full automation will surface noise; we prioritize high-signal features first and keep a human-in-the-loop review for top candidates
Speed vs. engineering cost: Building a robust ingestion pipeline takes weeks; initial approach uses lighter-weight scraping and scheduled batch jobs to validate concept
Breadth vs. depth: We will track a broad set of ~50 seeds but only run deep runtime validation on top 5-10 candidates to conserve budget
risks: Signal manipulation: public metrics can be gamed or spiked; need heuristics for persistence and cross-signal validation
Hidden engineering debt: unexpected model artifacts (custom ops, kv-cache variants) may delay onboarding and skew prioritization
Legal/licensing surprises: some permissive-seeming repos have downstream redistribution restrictions — legal review lag could stall pilots
